title: Lab Interpretation
sources: Standard laboratory medicine; LabRef (model, not source)

changelog.change: Initial entry — electrolyte replacement dosing needs review-tier 1.

summary: Common lab patterns, a micro quick-reference, and electrolyte replacement guidance.

items: Leukocytosis with left shift → bacterial infection / stress demargination
Cytopenias → marrow suppression, sequestration, consumption, dilution

Anemia — work up by MCV: microcytic (iron deficiency, thalassemia, chronic disease), normocytic (acute blood loss, hemolysis, early chronic disease), macrocytic (B12/folate, alcohol, hypothyroid, MDS)

body.text: Gram stain morphology → likely organism → empiric coverage CLASS (not specific drugs/doses — those live in the Empiric Antibiotic Guide and must reflect your antibiogram). Gram-positive cocci in clusters → Staphylococcus; in chains → Streptococcus / Enterococcus. Gram-negative rods → Enterobacterales / Pseudomonas. Gram-negative diplococci → Neisseria.

rows: ~10 mEq IV raises serum K⁺ by ~0.1 mEq/L. Peripheral infusion ≤ 10 mEq/h (max ~20 mEq/h central, on a monitor). Replace magnesium concurrently — you can't fix K⁺ while Mg²⁺ is low.
1-2 g IV MgSO₄ over 1-2 h for mild-moderate deficiency; 2 g over 15 min for torsades or severe symptomatic hypomagnesemia.
0.08-0.16 mmol/kg (≈ 15-30 mmol) IV over 4-6 h for moderate hypophosphatemia; recheck and re-dose. Watch for hypocalcemia and renal impairment.

body.text: All infusion-rate limits assume normal renal function and continuous monitoring for the higher rates. Halve replacement in renal impairment and recheck sooner.
